history.period: Association with the seventh Sikh Guru (17th century - traditional account)
history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurdwara Sri Amb Sahib in Phase VIII, Mohali (opposite the bus stand, near the PCA Cricket Stadium) is associated with Guru Har Rai, the seventh Sikh Guru (hence 'Patshahi Satvi'). The tradition holds that a Sikh follower named Bhai Kuram was blessed by the Guru under a mango tree ('Amb' is Punjabi for mango) that unseasonally bore fruit; the tree is said to still stand and bear fruit year-round. The gurdwara runs a daily langar and a low-cost sarai for needy travellers, and draws large crowds on Gurpurabs. CSV TOWN WRONG: actual town Mohali (district Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar), not Chandigarh. Coordinates 30.71307, 76.71051 are APPROXIMATE (verify) - the geocoder matched a nearby Phase-8 gurdwara; the shrine is confirmed at Phase VIII, opposite the ISBT, near the stadium.

name: Gurdwara Sri Amb Sahib (Patshahi Satvi)
town_description: Mohali (officially Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar) is a planned city and district headquarters in Punjab, forming the western part of the Chandigarh Tricity with Chandigarh and Panchkula. It is known for the PCA (Bindra) Cricket Stadium, the IT corridor around Phase 8, and the inter-state bus terminus. Gurdwara Amb Sahib stands in Phase 8, opposite the bus stand, close to the cricket stadium.
